steps.text: Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Stir in the shell pasta and cook until tender but firm to the bite, 10 to 11 minutes; drain.
Combine peas, Cheddar, ham, onion, mayonnaise, oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add cooked pasta and stir to coat. Cover and refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Shell Salad
raw_recipe.description: Tasty pasta salad with ham, peas, cubes of Cheddar cheese, and shell pasta with a lemony, mayonnaise-based dressing. Perfect for picnics and potlucks.
raw_recipe.name: Ham and Shell Salad

review.reviewBody: My kids really like this salad. I do add a little finely chopped red onion, and if the shredded cheddar cheese is on sale I do use that, (not a big deal to swap out for the cubed cheese) and sometimes to save time I also use a bottled salad dressing. My youngest daughter really likes this with bacon ranch salad dressing!!!

I’m eating this now. It’s really good! It’s great to use up the small amounts of pastas I have left from other dishes. Mine has elbows and shells. Frozen Peas went into the pot a few minutes after the pasta. Thanks to another reviewer, I used white pepper and a dash of cayenne, skipped the cheese.

Used one green onion (not an onion fan); omitted salt and other seasonings. Made dressing with 3Tbsp. Miracle Whip + 2 Tbsp. Kraft Sun Dried Tomato & Red Pepper dressing. Added more dressing to make it moister. Very delicious!
Recipe was good. I doubled the dressing recipe. I used cellentani pasta and added a diced green pepper.

Made with the ranch dressing added 16 oz. bag of California blend frozen veggies that was a definite plus! used shredded cheese only cause that was what I had. don't skimp on the dressing. I made on Thursday and served on Friday I think it's better with more time in the fridge. There is room to play with this recipe and make it to your flavor favorites. Will definitely make again.

Easy main course salad to make in advance for an anticipated busy evening; added cauliflower to pasta pot to increase vegetable servings. Did not use the oil, but did add cucumber Ranch to the mix. Also used McCormick Salad Supreme to amp up the flavor. Have made multiple times usually using the frozen peas and carrots. Very flexible as different cheeses work well. Easy and tasty. Great as leftovers too.

This was very good! I stirred together the dressing first and then added the ham, cheese, and veggies. I used an entire 12 oz. package of peas and 2TB onion. I left all other measurements the same. I rinsed my pasta with cold water and added it last, but I think next time I'll add them first to make sure they get good and coated with the dressing. I may add 50% more dressing, but it really was wonderful as is written. Very tasty!

I find this is very good because I cook for someone with dysphagia. His gullet is about half its normal size because of surgery after a fall. The only change I made was to shred the pasta, cheese and ham. Chunks of anything just don't work, but the basic composition is fine.

This is the foundation for a good pasta salad. I added cayenne pepper, paprika, Cole slaw dressing and some ranch dressing as well as a wee bit of bacon fat instead of the oil. I think you could omit the cheese or shred it as other reviewers mentioned. Onion is a must. I added these items as it started out too dry ( not enough dressing) and bland. Would make again, but as mentioned, as the base for the salad.

Enjoyed this salad did add red bell pepper, small dice celery for crunch ,used green onion not regular also saw no reason to use the oil, liked it and will add it to summer menu.Thank you ramblinrose. Thinking maybe next time instead of ham will use tiny salad shrimp.

I used macaroni, 2 tbs. ranch dressing, and equal parts olive oil mayo and reduced fat sour cream and omitted the oil for the sauce base for this recipe. I did NOT add SALT because the HAM has plenty. I substituted white pepper and a dash of cayenne for the black pepper. YUM! It's dishes like this that I end up eating most of and NOT taking for a pot luck.
I didn't have shells so I made it with mini bow ties. Quick and easy to make. Taking it to a church picnic today
Its good, super easy, and could be tweaked about a million different ways. Thanks for sharing.
Super easy to make, disappears very quickly. It has only been a month and I think I have made it four times already - everybody loves this recipe!
Very simple yet good.
Great salad I doubled the dressing mix to make sure it was moist enough. I've made this salad a few times now and it definitely delicious and doesn't last long.
Quick, easy and delicious

Made as directed with one change: I used spring green onions because that was all I had on hand, and I think the flavor was better for it. Will certainly make again. It was easy, fast, very tasty and delicious.

Oops!!! My review got cut off. Anyways...I love this!!! Very delicious. It’s a lighter pasta salad. I will say when I mixed the dressing it looked curdled but it mixed up well in the pasta,onion,peas,cheese & ham. It’s drier so don’t be surprised but I guess I like that. You could always make extra dressing if u like it wetter. Definitely will be making this again! Thanks!! ??

Delicious and easy to make. I made it according to the directions except I omitted the salt. I used avocado oil for the vegetable oil. It can be enjoyed warm, room temperature or cold. Make s a wonderful summer light main dish or side salad. I will definitely make this often.
